requirements.expectation: Issues a registration token, registers and onboards a disposable author Bot, and bootstraps the local Human principal before any business request; every later call carries the Human mock identity headers.

Registers the scripted coverage Provider (static_bearer auth, protocol 2.0, native_tool coordination, webhook pointed at the owned mock sink), publishes driver and reviewer provider Bots under provider_admin_token, and completes the driver-to-reviewer friendship request/accept.
Uploads the unchanged 2174-byte indentation-regression incident YAML as Draft revision 1; the saved revision and content_hash must equal the fixture bytes and their SHA-256 digest.
The revision reference remains CLI-compatible, exposes exactly schemaVersion/draftId/revision/readToken, and uses a fixed non-secret legacy placeholder rather than an authority grant.
The /api/v1 preview returns the stored YAML byte-for-byte (no re-indentation or rewriting) without accepting a separate read-token grant and pins content_hash and revision to the uploaded values.
Validation through the unambiguous V1 revision path runs against the same stored revision; validity, content_hash and revision stay bound instead of re-parsing supplied input.

Both the V1 preview and validation surface reject a missing/unknown revision with 404 DRAFT_REFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE; the fixed placeholder readToken does not help and no alternate draft resource is inferred.
A non-integer revision path segment and a validate body attempting to replace the stored YAML both fail with 400 DRAFT_INPUT.

The browser API derives the operator identity from the configured Human auth chain (/me returns user_id and display_name) and every browser submission must present the matching X-BCS-Expected-User header.

The owned Bot selector (/bots/mine) returns exactly the user's registered Bots and the collaborator candidates of the chosen driver Bot include the accepted friend, so the originator is user-selected rather than assistant-chosen.

The group launch body applies the edited title to the Draft YAML, selects the driver Bot as originator and driver, pins the state_machine collaboration strategy, and binds writer/reviewer/publisher roles to explicit Bot actor ids.

POST /groups without browser context, with a cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site header, with a changed expected account, or with a duplicated expected-user header is refused with 403 browser_context_required or user_context_changed.
Author Bot credentials, an Actor header and an invalid X-Avernet-Principal cannot impersonate the Human at the browser submission boundary (401 unauthenticated).
Group creation succeeds with an initial navigation session; the persisted group keeps the chosen driver Bot, the user-edited YAML and the explicit role bindings without substituting the author Bot.
After the group is created, the historical shared card still returns the original immutable source bytes; group launch never mutates the Draft.
The author revokes the revision share (204); afterwards both preview and validate through the old reference fail with 404 DRAFT_REFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE.

Cleanup deletes the group, the Draft, every disposable Bot (provider Bots via provider admin token, the author Bot via the bot API) and disables the scripted Provider; any cleanup failure fails the story instead of leaking state.
